note: Kern County campground in two loops beside the lower Kern River near Lake Ming, NE of Bakersfield; dry camping, generators allowed. The county warns that the river's currents drown people every year. --Claude
summary: Kern River Campground (Kern County): $24 peak / $12 off-peak confirmed, reservable on the county's own system (14-night max, 2 sites per customer), 49 sites 30-55 ft, no hookups, showers + dump, year-round. Riverfront downgraded to riverview: the operator types every site 'Non-Waterfront' and a continuous riparian belt screens the river. Note rewritten (the 'some with hookups' claim was wrong). Website dead; phone added.
flags: WATERFRONT: riverfront -> riverview (downgrade; not --AWH). The river is wide enough for riverfront (~35-60 m on Esri at the camp), and the riverside rows (map sites 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25 on the west loop; 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50 on the north loop; all sold by the night) sit ~25-45 m from the water (e.g. an RV at ~35.4368,-118.8767 is ~33 m from the water's edge at ~35.4371,-118.8770). But a continuous riparian tree belt runs along the bank between every pad and the water, and the county's own reservation system types all 49 sites 'Non-Waterfront' (it does sell 'Waterfront' sites at its Buena Vista campground). No site photo exists. The county describes 'the campground overlooking the Kern River', so riverview; a reviewer could go to not waterfront if the trees block the view from the pads.
